examples.japanese: {美術館|びじゅつかん}に{油彩画|ゆさいが}が{飾|かざ}られている。
examples.english: Oil paintings are displayed in the art museum.

examples.japanese: この{油彩画|ゆさいが}は{十九世紀|じゅうきゅうせいき}のフランスで{描|えが}かれた。
examples.english: This oil painting was painted in nineteenth-century France.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{趣味|しゅみ}で{油彩画|ゆさいが}を{描|か}いており、{自宅|じたく}には{何十枚|なんじゅうまい}もの{作品|さくひん}がある。
examples.english: My grandfather paints oil paintings as a hobby, and there are dozens of works at his home.

notes:
Refers specifically to a painting created with oil-based paints. The formal term for what is colloquially called {油絵|あぶらえ}. Oil painting as a technique was introduced to Japan during the Meiji period.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {油彩画|ゆさいが}を{描|か}く: to paint an oil painting
- {油彩画|ゆさいが}{展|てん}: oil painting exhibition
- {小品|しょうひん}の{油彩画|ゆさいが}: a small oil painting

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {油絵|あぶらえ}: oil painting — the everyday, colloquial equivalent
- {水彩画|すいさいが}: watercolor painting — uses water-soluble paints; lighter and more transparent than oil
- {油彩|ゆさい}: oil painting (technique/medium) — refers to the method rather than the finished work
